stories.h: Recursive Superintelligence signs $410 million compute deal with Amazon Web Services
stories.s: The multiyear compute commitment signals a shift toward large, long‑term cloud spend for self‑improving AI and could attract other foundation‑level labs to similar deals, speeding product timelines and infrastructure ambitions.
b: Multi‑year compute deal with Amazon Web Services valued around $410 million (TechCrunch report)
RSI emerged from stealth in May with about $650 million in funding
Socher expects the deal to be the first of many and anticipates early products by October
AWS involvement has no investment component and includes co‑developing infrastructure tailored for RSI, per the report
body: Recursive Superintelligence announced a multiyear compute deal with Amazon Web Services as it scales its self‑improving AI research agenda, the company said in a TechCrunch report. The arrangement is described as a long‑term commitment meant to provide flexibility as RSI builds out its open‑ended AI systems at scale.

TechCrunch notes that RSI’s $410 million outlay represents the bulk of the company’s fundraising to date, and Socher said he expects this to be the first of many such deals as the company grows. Socher told TechCrunch that today’s announcement is likely to be one of the smaller compute agreements the company signs in the coming years.

The company’s emphasis on self‑improving AI means more budget going into compute rather than traditional headcount and operations, with Socher saying, “For us, it’s less about headcount and more about agent count.”

There is no investment component to AWS’s involvement in the deal, but AWS is expected to commit significant resources to RSI’s needs and co‑develop infrastructure tailored for these types of companies, according to Jason Bennett, AWS VP for startups and venture capital.

RSI’s leadership positions self‑improvement as a potential inflection point for AI progress, though coverage notes that the exact requirements and timelines remain ambiguous as more labs pursue the idea. Socher emphasized tangible progress, telling TechCrunch that users could see “the earliest examples before the end of the year,” with a concrete reveal around October.
Overall, RSI’s leadership frames the deal as a platform shift designed to accelerate product development and deployment, positioning AWS as a strategic partner rather than a traditional investor.
srcTitles: Recursive Superintelligence signs $410 million compute deal with Amazon

stories.h: Gemini API managed agents default to 3.6 Flash with environment hooks
stories.s: Developers can prototype autonomous agent workflows inside a sandbox, using free tier access and token caps to control costs.
b: Gemini 3.6 Flash is the default for Managed Agents in Gemini API.
Free tier access is available for managed agents on projects without active billing.
Max total tokens (max_total_tokens) can cap usage; the example shows 10,000 tokens.
Explicit model pinning is supported via agent_config.model, including Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite for lower cost.
body: Google's blog introduces Managed Agents in the Gemini API, noting that Gemini 3.6 Flash is now the default for these agents and that new environment hooks let you block, lint, or audit tool calls inside the sandbox.

The post explains that you can explicitly select models by passing agent_config.model, with Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite available for lower cost and the option to pin to a preferred model. It also highlights how scripts can be integrated into the agent workflow using the antigravity-preview-05-2026 release tag.

Environment hooks are a key feature, described as a way to run custom scripts before or after every tool call inside the sandbox. The example configuration shows pre_tool_execution and post_tool_execution hooks that can, for instance, enforce security checks or code formatting.

Google provides real‑world context for production use, citing an AI-native investment bank example where a post_tool_execution hook triggers a validation pipeline inside the sandbox to verify assets like logos and publish an approved manifest. The post also notes that managed agents can run multi-turn autonomous loops, which necessitates budgeting controls and pause-and-resume behavior if limits are reached.

The article also covers budgeting and scheduling: managed agents are now available on free tier projects, and a max_total_tokens setting caps overall consumption. If the limit is hit, execution pauses with status 'incomplete' and can be resumed later using a previous_interaction_id with a fresh budget, while recurring tasks can be set with scheduled triggers to reuse the same sandbox.
srcTitles: Gemini API Managed Agents: 3.6 Flash, hooks, and more

body: Google’s latest AI features in Search aim to simplify dinner‑party planning by enabling users to visualize tablescapes, design menus, brainstorm recipes, locate drink pairings, and curate playlists that sync with preferred apps. The update focuses on helping you plan not just what to cook, but how to present and enjoy the overall experience.

Users can leverage Nano Banana in AI Mode to visualize how a table could look, while AI Mode helps brainstorm menu options and suggest drinks that complement chosen dishes. The AI tools are designed to streamline creative decisions, from theme to dish selection, so hosts can focus on guest experience.

Once decisions are made, AI Mode can generate a printable menu or shareable design, and it can connect with Canva to support on‑the‑fly design tasks as part of the planning flow. In addition, AI‑driven recipe results include richer details at the top of responses—images plus data such as the recipe creator’s name, ratings, and ingredient counts.

The article also notes that you can tie searches to your existing app ecosystem, for example by saving a playlist to YouTube Music or generating menu visuals you can print or share with guests, illustrating a broader push to make Google Search a planning hub for real‑world activities.

College students are highlighted as a demographic trending toward using these tools to remix dorm room spaces, with Google pointing to Search trends as evidence of growing interest in offline, real‑world planning.

stories.h: Samsung chip workers jump ship to SK Hynix after bigger bonuses
stories.s: The exodus signals a high-stakes talent war that could determine who leads AI memory chips and how quickly supply and pricing shift for AI accelerators.
b: SK Hynix is paying about $476,000 per employee this year, mostly in cash, to lure talent from Samsung
Samsung’s bonuses by division vary: memory division about $400,000 per employee vs. foundry division about $135,000
81.5% of employees in Samsung’s foundry division reportedly want to move to another company within two years, and more than 200 union members left for SK Hynix over the past four months

In H1 2026 SK Hynix added 2,152 employees to staff the expansion, and both firms topped $1 trillion in market value in May, with SK Hynix briefly dethroning Samsung as Korea’s most valuable company in June
body: MIT Technology Review reports that Samsung’s chip workers are jumping ship to SK Hynix as the AI hardware boom fuels a fierce talent war. Lee, an engineer in Samsung’s semiconductor division, describes coworkers applying to SK Hynix and says his team lead tells them to jump ship to SK Hynix, a message that has spread through the office as workers seek better pay and prospects.

The report notes that Samsung struck a deal in May to pay out 10.5% of the semiconductor division’s operating profits to employees as bonuses for 10 years, mostly in stock that vests over three years. In contrast, SK Hynix is paying a much larger upfront package: roughly $476,000 per employee this year, mostly in cash, a figure that dwarfs Samsung’s payouts. Within Samsung, bonuses vary by division: the memory division pays about $400,000 per employee this year, while the foundry division pays roughly $135,000.

Labor dynamics are central to the tale. Samsung’s labor union talks have yielded gains in other areas, but workers say the discrepancy in bonuses helps explain the defections. The Samsung labor union chief, Choi Seung-ho, has said that more than 200 members have left for SK Hynix in the past four months, and a June survey reported that 81.5% of foundry division employees want to move to another company within two years. Some employees also discuss their plans on Blind, an anonymous workplace forum, underscoring a broad morale challenge at Samsung’s chip plants.

The broader market context adds pressure to this talent war. MIT Technology Review notes that SK Hynix now leads the global market for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips, a technology central to AI accelerators, while Samsung has been scrambling to catch up. Both companies topped $1 trillion in market value in May, and SK Hynix briefly dethroned Samsung as Korea’s most valuable company in June. To staff expansion tied to this growth, SK Hynix reported adding 2,152 employees in the first half of 2026. In parallel, the AI spending boom and China’s progress in advanced chipmaking have fed a stock-market reaction: Bloomberg, via Techmeme, reported that South Korea’s KOSPI fell more than 11%, with Samsung down around 11% and SK Hynix down about 12%.

What happens next could reshape the AI hardware supply chain. MIT Technology Review frames the outcome as a race to dominate the next generation of HBMs, with the winner potentially locking in talent, boosting production capacity, and influencing pricing as demand for AI chips remains volatile.
srcTitles: Samsung’s chip workers are jumping ship to rival SK Hynix

stories.h: Fish Audio raises $50M seed to build AI voice models for creators and enterprises
stories.s: The seed funding underscores growing demand for expressive, controllable AI voices across creators and enterprises, while also spotlighting governance questions around consent, licensing, and ownership of trained voices.
b: Seed round of $50 million led by Coreline Ventures and Capital Today (plus participation from 359 Capital, Parable, and others)
Fish Audio reports $21 million ARR and over 8 million users, with more than 15,000 natural language controls across its models
Five models launched in the past year (four speech generation, one speech‑to‑text); three generation models open‑sourced, latest S2.1 Pro is API‑based and paid
The company automated its voice‑ownership DMCA takedown flow to under 3 minutes for consented voice removals; creators can submit proof of ownership for fast removal
body: Fish Audio, a Palo Alto startup, announced a $50 million seed round led by Coreline Ventures and Capital Today to expand its library of AI voice models for creators and enterprises. The company aims to support a broad range of use cases from expressive character voices to automated customer interactions, with a library that currently features more than 15,000 natural language controls.

Since its public launch last year, Fish Audio has grown to over 8 million users across its open‑source and hosted offerings and reports annual recurring revenue of about $21 million. The startup has rolled out five models over the past year—four speech generation models and one speech‑to‑text model—and has open‑sourced three generation models, while the latest S2.1 Pro model is available only through its paid API.

Fish Audio’s CEO and co‑founder Rissa Cao indicated a broad portfolio of voice applications, with customers including companies like HeyGen, Sanas and Plaud that use its voices for different needs—realism for avatars, expressiveness for games, or natural voices for voice agents.

The company has faced earlier concerns when creators claimed their voices were uploaded without consent; Fish Audio has since automated its DMCA removal flow, allowing creators to submit a sample or contract to prove ownership and have their voice taken down within minutes. Investors stressed that consent, transparency, and clear licensing are essential to building trust in community‑driven voice ecosystems.

Looking ahead, Fish Audio plans to release an audio understanding model this year and is also working on a speech‑to‑speech model, as it competes in a crowded market with players like ElevenLabs and Krisp.
srcTitles: Fish Audio raises $52M seed to build AI voice models for creators and enterprises

stories.s: AI Mode in Search could pull more people into offline activities and deepen engagement with Google’s ecosystem by guiding real‑world planning, bookings, and shopping through connected apps.

body: Google’s AI Mode in Search is positioned as a tool for people who want to spend more time in the real world by simplifying how they plan activities and events. The feature set includes finding local classes that fit a user’s schedule, shopping for specific gear, practicing hobbies, and booking tickets for events.

Personal Intelligence enables AI Mode to securely connect across Google apps so responses feel more personalized and aligned with a user’s calendar and preferences. This creates a tighter loop between planning and execution, helping users turn ideas into real‑world actions.

Google also highlights current interest in offline activities, noting queries like “adult tennis lessons,” “trail running,” “hiking,” and “run club” are trending, with demand for digital detox guidance up more than 110% year over year.

Canvas within AI Mode lets users create practical guides, such as a chess strategy memo, by selecting Canvas from the AI Mode plus menu and asking for a few easy‑to‑remember moves; users can use Canvas to practice by building a game simulation against a computer.

The company also describes ways to use AI Mode to find and book nearby events, and to design materials like flyers in Canva from within the Search results, illustrating how AI Mode consolidates planning tools across apps for real‑world activities.
